title: Optimization of Moringa oleifera seed ash for domestic wastewater COD removal
content:
Abstract

Most studies on Moringa oleifera the treatment of the water treatment have focused on the usage of raw seed powder as a coagulant. In this work, we used the thermally activated seed ash (prepared at 700°C for 7 h) as an adsorbent to remove chemical oxygen demand (COD) from domestic wastewater. Many experiments were conducted to study the effects of contact time (15–120 min), adsorbent dose (0.5–5.5 g/L), and pH (4–10). The initial COD of the wastewater was 193.2 mg/L. By employing response surface methodology with Box–Behnken design, the best conditions for COD removal were observed to be 111 min contact time, 5.25 g/L adsorbent dosage, and pH 6.73. At this stage, the maximum COD removal was obtained as 88.6% and brought down the COD level of the effluent as close as 23 mg/L to the CPCB discharge standard of 30 mg/L. Statistical results revealed that contact time and adsorbent dosage strongly affected COD removal (p <0.05), whereas pH had a lesser numerical effect. The SEM analysis provided clear evidence about the visible change in the surface of the adsorbent material. Furthermore, the results of EDX analysis revealed elemental difference in the sample, confirming pollution removal from the waste stream.
